Definition: from a compound of the base of G3725 and a derivative of G5087; a limit-placing, i.e. (concretely) boundary-line:--bound.
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, horothesía means a setting of boundaries. It occurs just once, in Acts.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple here: horothesía means a setting of boundaries, and I do not stretch it further.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
